No, it does not use a database transaction. According to [[write-journal]], the guarded write journal provides transactional semantics **without needing a database**. 

The journal itself acts as the transaction log, kept in memory for the duration of a single run. If a run fails, it can roll back all recorded writes in reverse order by restoring previous file content or deleting newly created files — all managed through the journal mechanism itself, not through a database transaction layer.
